title: Exception Lifecycle (try-except-else-finally & raise) Simulator
description: Visualizing how Python intercepts a manual raise statement, bypasses normal execution, branches to the matching except handler, and guarantees execution of the finally block.
codeLines: if mark < 0 or mark > 100: raise ValueError('Mark must be between 0 and 100')
except ValueError as error: print('Invalid mark:', error)

steps.explanation: Incoming raw input string is received as '150'.
Entering the try block to monitor for runtime exceptions.
int('150') converts successfully to the integer value 150.
Validation condition (mark > 100) evaluates to True. The program intentionally raises a ValueError with message 'Mark must be between 0 and 100'.
Normal flow in try is interrupted. Python skips line 5 (else logic) and jumps directly into except ValueError as error.
steps.output: Invalid mark: Mark must be between 0 and 100

steps.explanation: The finally block executes unconditionally to ensure clean completion.
